utility.notes: The City of Industry is confirmed to be within SCE's distribution service territory.

value.name: Southern California Edison (SCE)
value.notes: Clean Power Alliance's own homepage states it serves '38 communities across Los Angeles and Ventura counties' and names each one individually via its site's community directory; City of Industry is not among the named communities. No other Los Angeles/Ventura County CCA serving City of Industry was found, so Southern California Edison (SCE) is recorded as both the distribution and generation utility.

permit_authority.value: Los Angeles County Department of Public Works, Building and Safety Division
permit_authority.notes: The City of Industry does not operate its own building department; per the city's own site, all building, electrical, mechanical, and plumbing permits — including solar — are issued by LA County Building & Safety, operating out of a satellite office within City of Industry.

permit_url.notes: The fetched page confirms the contract-city arrangement with LA County and the online BSOP portal, but did not itemize solar-specific requirements, fees, or timelines.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this dataset.

value.name: California SGIP - current category and budget check required
value.description: New applications and waitlist applications for ratepayer-funded SGIP budgets closed on December 30, 2025. New AB 209 applications have a June 30, 2028 deadline. The 2026 SGIP rate table publishes $3.10/W for solar and $1.10/Wh for storage in applicable Residential Solar and Storage Equity categories. Household eligibility and live budget availability vary by category and program administrator; check the official Program Metrics tracker before relying on an incentive.
value.eligibility: Eligibility varies by 2026 SGIP budget category, program administrator, property, income/pathway, project rules, and live funding availability.

battery_programs.notes: SGIP program data refreshed on 2026-08-26 from the official 2026 Handbook and live Program Metrics. Earlier locality records contained 2025 opening/availability language. This record does not assert household eligibility, reservation availability, or a guaranteed incentive; current category and program-administrator status must be checked before reliance.

value.name: Permit application meeting Building Code Section 106.4 requirements
Plans conforming to the checklist and standard plans in LA County Building Code Manual 6807, Article 1 (per the California Solar Permitting Guidebook)

required_documents.notes: Per LA County Code Title 26 (Building Code), Chapter 68 (Expedited Permitting for Small Residential Rooftop Solar Energy Systems), Sections 6803 and 6807.3. City of Industry contracts LA County Department of Public Works, Building and Safety Division for permitting, so LA County's own code chapter directly governs.

value: A single combination inspection covers the structural, electrical, and plumbing components of the solar installation

Evidence of correct installation/labeling must be provided at inspection (the Building Official may require exposure of roof-mount fastening, panel grounding/bonding, and module/inverter nameplates if not otherwise verifiable)
If the system fails inspection, subsequent inspections are authorized until the work is approved
inspection_steps.notes: Per LA County Code Chapter 68, Section 6806 (Inspections).

value.notes: LA County Code Chapter 68, Section 6803: 'Upon receipt of a complete small residential rooftop solar energy system application, plan check review will be completed within one to three business days.'

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited Permitting for Small Residential Rooftop Solar Energy Systems (LA County Code Title 26, Chapter 68)
other_conditions: System must be installed on a one- or two-family dwelling
Solar panel/module array must not exceed the maximum legal building height per LA County Planning and Zoning Code

Photovoltaic systems must be listed for the application per the Electrical Code; solar thermal systems must be certified by the Solar Rating and Certification Corporation or an approved listing agency
